headline: Senate resolution that would have asked the State Department for a report on Israel's human rights practices did not advance.
what_it_does: This resolution would have asked the State Department to give Congress a public (unclassified) statement on Israel's human rights practices, under a section of the Foreign Assistance Act of 1961. The statement would have covered credible information on the alleged killings of nine named U.S. citizens, and any other U.S. citizens, by Israeli forces or settlers since 2022. That would have included possible suspects and any steps Israeli authorities took to investigate. It also would have covered U.S. citizens held in Israeli prisons and Palestinian children held in Israeli military detention in the West Bank.

who_it_affects.how: The department would have been asked to prepare and send Congress a detailed public statement on Israel's human rights practices.

who_it_affects.group: Families of U.S. citizens killed in Israel or the West Bank since 2022
who_it_affects.how: The report would have gathered information on the killings, possible suspects, and any investigations.

who_it_affects.group: U.S. citizens held in Israeli prisons
who_it_affects.how: The report would have included an assessment of their situation.

who_it_affects.group: Palestinian children in Israeli military detention in the West Bank
who_it_affects.how: The report would have described their human rights situation.
